title: Quadriplegia, paraplegia, monoplegia and spinal cord disorders
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's paralysis or spinal cord condition (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for spinal cord injury.

HPI
Pt is a 56 y.o. female presenting for routine follow-up. Pt has a long-standing hx of incomplete quadriplegia resulting from a spinal cord injury several years ago. Pt uses a power wheelchair for all mobility. She reports stable status today with no new concerns regarding motor function or sensation in upper or lower extremities. Denies any recent falls or changes in skin integrity.

Medication List
None reported.

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Vitals: BP 122/78, HR 72, RR 16, Temp 98.6F.
Neuro: Pt demonstrates incomplete motor function at the C5-C7 level. Strength is limited in distal extremities. Sensation is diminished in lower body.
MSK: No new deformities noted.
Skin: Intact.

Assessment
1. Incomplete quadriplegia, C5-C7 level. Stable.

Plan
1. Continue current activity level.
2. Follow up in 6 months for routine reassessment.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, MD
05/14/2026

distractors.why: The level and completeness are documented.
